acceptance.requirement: A versioned machine policy ranks priority, downstream unlock, critical path, starvation, acceptance completion, validation placement, and stable task identity without input-order or issue-number authority.
Starvation eventually advances a same-priority eligible task but never crosses an unmet stage or semantic dependency.
Acceptance-group completion value never outranks a higher-priority or security-critical stage task.
The selector returns the deterministic maximal safe batch, exactly fills fifteen slots from twenty independent tasks, selects exactly N safe tasks, and never exceeds available slots.
Writers sharing an explicit owner/write conflict key or issue worktree write key are never selected together.
Semantic dependencies and conflict facts remain separate, and conflict keys require investigated evidence rather than path-prefix inference alone.
Active resource leases block only matching explicit keys; a long task occupies only its own slot and resources while unrelated ready tasks continue.
Only legal stage tasks are selectable; DAG agents and tasks with unmet receipt prerequisites cannot fill slots.
One issue worktree has at most one writer; ordinary code implementers cannot own UI paths; behavior and UX verifiers remain read-only.
A read-only verifier may run beside a nonconflicting writer only against a frozen candidate identity.
Every lease binds owner, attempt, acquisition, expiry/recovery rule, key set, and digest; duplicate ownership and tampering fail closed.
Only the matching attempt releases a lease and an expired lease requires durable recovery evidence before another attempt acquires it.
Selected, deferred, structured reasons, blockers, rank components, and batchDigest are independently validated and root cannot reorder or rewrite the machine batch.
The six frontier and dispatch fields are one required unit; deleting one is incomplete and deleting all six cannot bypass dispatch validation.
The #1816 verified frontier binds complete conflict, resource, and candidate facts into each dispatch task; deleting a shared conflict cannot make two writers co-selectable.
A root-only delivery action blocks only its repository or explicit keys and does not freeze the other repository or independent stages.
A group proposal carries complete qualification evidence and falls back for unrelated members or hidden dependency/order violations.
A group session occupies a slot only with an active member and cannot reduce work conservation or starve an independent ready task.
Group evidence uses finite typed values in bounded ranges, and independent memberOrder is canonical, order-sensitive, and cannot be reversed or replaced by a bogus permutation.
The live-bound FsusUI 267-279 sample preserves its explicit dependencies, investigated owner surfaces, P0/P1/P2 facts, ready stage set, writer conflict, and explainable maximal batch.
